title: Write authority
summary: Lane inspection permits chained read-only Git calls, simple file reads and directory changes. File reads include nl; test and [ predicates also qualify as reads. Every segment is checked; mixed writes, redirects and command substitutions retain ordinary lane authority. Inline sed/awk programs are data, while input and script files remain path operands. Git calls with environment assignment prefixes or global -c, --config-env or --exec-path options do not qualify as reads; ordinary status and calls using -C or --git-dir still qualify. Configuration options remain parsed for write-target detection. A Yoke command chained with lane Git inspection is allowed only without any cd segment or lane-path operand on the Yoke command. Git fetch updates shared repository metadata rather than main source; pull still changes main. Python joinpath writes resolve only when the receiver and all arguments are known. Non-path mkdir, touch and truncate option values do not become write targets.
